question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the roots of $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}+2x-8}{{x}^{2}-9x+18}$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}} $\,$
and
$\,\,x=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(x)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(x)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+2x-8}{{x}^{2}-9x+18}=0.
$$

First, we factor $f(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}+2x-8}{{x}^{2}-9x+18} \\  & =\frac{(x+4)(x-2)}{(x-3)(x-6)}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =-4,\,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to $f(x)=0$, in ascending order, are $x=-4$ and $x=2.$
